error_note: A low anti-GM1b ganglioside IgG titer is the normal state and says nothing about immune function; it is bridged through a near-root immune phenotype to a disease with no link to this autoantibody.

Low LH fits the hypogonadotropic hypogonadism of X-linked AHC, but the code is a third specimen after an unspecified (XXX) challenge, so 'low' is undefined without knowing the stimulus and its response criteria.
Hypercalcemia (with nephrocalcinosis) is reported only occasionally in glucose-galactose malabsorption and is shared by many diseases; calcium is not a test for this disorder.
Nelson syndrome arises after bilateral adrenalectomy, so cortisol is not elevated (ACTH is); the 'very frequent' hypercortisolism annotation appears carried over from Cushing disease.

Hypoglycemia in MEN1 comes from insulinoma in a minority and is typically fasting; a low value 6 hours into a glucose tolerance test more often reflects reactive hypoglycemia, and hypoglycemia is shared by some 200 diseases.

Suppressed C-peptide occurs only in the very rare IGF2-mediated hypoglycemia of solitary fibrous tumor (Doege-Potter) and is shown during spontaneous hypoglycemia, not after an unspecified (XXX) challenge.
A low mold-mix specific IgE is a normal non-sensitised result, not an abnormal immunoglobulin concentration, and has no bearing on Schimke immuno-osseous dysplasia.
Brucella IgM serology is specific to brucellosis and does not demonstrate bacteremia; routing it through generic 'Bacteremia' to listeriosis loses the pathogen identity.
A low Aspergillus niger precipitin titer is the normal result and is not a measure of immunoglobulin class concentration; it does not relate to alpha-heavy chain disease.
The disease record states hyperglycemia is explicitly NOT a feature of essential fructosuria, yet a positive association was emitted.
Thyroid autoimmunity is somewhat more prevalent in resistance to thyroid hormone beta, but TPO antibodies are neither diagnostic nor characteristic and the 30-79% frequency looks overstated.
Hematuria is a very rare (<5%) feature of Castleman disease and is shared by well over a hundred diseases.
A low Johnson grass IgE is a normal result, not an immunoglobulin concentration abnormality; the target is an obsolete MONDO term for a serum protein polymorphism rather than a disease.

Low C-peptide in solitary fibrous tumor is a very rare paraneoplastic finding seen during hypoglycemia; a low glucagon-stimulated C-peptide instead reads as beta-cell failure, so the challenge changes what low means.
Low LDL cholesterol is reported in very few ALG6-CDG patients (<5%) and is not a diagnostic or characteristic finding.
A normal asialo-GM1 IgG titer excludes only that one antibody (and one isotype); the phenotype covers all anti-ganglioside antibodies (GM1, GD1a, GQ1b and others), so it cannot be ruled out.

Hypoketosis during fasting hypoglycemia is characteristic of MCAD deficiency, but the code is a LOINC Part with no specimen or property, and 'decreased' is inappropriately low relative to the hypoglycemia rather than below a reference interval.
A low cattail-specific IgE is the normal non-sensitised state and does not indicate an abnormal circulating immunoglobulin concentration.

C-peptide 3 hours after a glucose load is a stimulated value; whether it is 'high' needs timepoint-specific criteria, so it does not straightforwardly show the baseline phenotype of elevated circulating C-peptide.

The content is right (alloisoleucine is undetectable, distinguishing this BCAT2 disorder from MSUD), but a pertinent negative is coded as a biomarker with expected result 'other', which does not convey 'not detected'.
Ectopic ACTH secretion occurs in only a small minority of bronchial neuroendocrine tumors, and the code is a 2-hour sample after an unspecified (XXX) challenge, where 'high' is undefined.
ALT may rise with the multi-organ injury of systemic monochloroacetate poisoning, but it is a nonspecific marker of hepatocellular injury and not a characteristic finding of this poisoning.
A pure-tone threshold at one frequency in one ear characterises hearing loss but does not diagnose the genetic entity DFNB93, and one frequency/ear stands in for a whole audiometric battery.
The rpoB mutation result is a rifampin-resistance (drug-susceptibility) measurement, not the M. tuberculosis detection component that diagnoses tuberculosis; it bears on rifampin-resistant TB.
A single-frequency, single-ear pure-tone threshold documents severity of hearing loss; it does not diagnose DFNB35, which requires molecular testing, and is one narrow component of audiometry.
Elevated C3 acylcarnitine is the right newborn-screening marker for methylmalonic acidemia, but the code is a LOINC Part (analyte only, no specimen or property), not a reportable test.

A normal total leukocyte count cannot rule out 'Abnormal leukocyte count', whose subclasses include neutropenia, lymphopenia and other differential abnormalities that can sum to a normal total, as the curator text itself concedes.
A high total/HDL ratio can result from low HDL alone with normal total cholesterol, so the ratio does not indicate hypercholesterolemia; the band also has no numeric bound.
A single eGFR below 60 gives the GFR category but does not establish chronic kidney disease, which requires persistence for more than 3 months; the same value occurs in acute kidney injury.

The low hemoglobin bands are sound, but the CTCAE Grade 1 band is encoded as 100 g/L and above with no upper bound, so as written normal hemoglobin values fall in an anemia band (the upper limit should be the sex-specific lower limit of normal).

Two of the three bands are analyser-specific treatment target ranges for children on levothyroxine, not reference intervals, and the method-agnostic LOINC code cannot select between cut-offs of 17.4 and 25.8 pmol/L, so the same result is and is not 'increased'.

MELD stratifies mortality in patients already known to have end-stage liver disease; a high score does not itself indicate chronic liver failure (acute liver failure, renal failure or anticoagulation also raise it).

A suppressed TSH is a screening finding that also occurs in subclinical thyrotoxicosis, physiological first-trimester suppression, central hypothyroidism and non-thyroidal illness; hyperthyroidism needs a free T4, as the curator text states.

Child-Pugh grades severity in a patient already known to have cirrhosis; it does not indicate cirrhosis, and the class A band (below 7) includes the minimum score of 5 that a person with normal liver function gets.
